# Thunderbird history batch 001: code and review style

Source snapshot: `Thunderbird comm checkout`, `origin/main` at `6ccc9d3f07d89f3d05984c119f20788417cecceb`, inspected 2026-10-06. The sample is the newest 100 first-parent, non-merge, human-authored commits. Skip 26 intervening locale-bump, vendored-Rust-sync, and build-trigger commits. The first included commit is `0b93f0f7a926ed94c8a0646f18b6734ec7cc0f6d`; the last is `24cde67836eaee8557c2e8dd0226f828acae70bd`. Continue the next batch from the last commit's first parent. Of 100 commits, 97 link to Phabricator; authenticated access worked for 58 reviews and was denied for 39 restricted reviews. Three have no Differential Revision link. Do not infer review guidance from inaccessible reviews. The 58 accessible histories contain 251 nonempty comments, including author replies and bots. The sample is weighted toward mailnews and one author (53 of 100 commits), so syntax patterns need more batches before they become project-wide guidance.

## Written project guidance

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` at this snapshot asks contributors to understand their changes, talk to maintainers or submit work in progress, keep changes focused, follow existing architecture and formatting, include tests and relevant docs, explain the approach, and write or humanize comments by hand. Its under-500-lines guidance is a preference, not a hard limit. Source: https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/blob/6ccc9d3f07d89f3d05984c119f20788417cecceb/CONTRIBUTING.md
- Thunderbird's documented local lint command is `../mach commlint path/to/files`. Source: https://developer.thunderbird.net/thunderbird-development/fixing-a-bug/lint-and-format-code

## Repeated code patterns in this batch

- 64 of 100 commits touch test files. Added code in 36 commits has a named `add_task(async function test...`; 53 add `Assert` calls; 24 add `registerCleanupFunction`. Treat these as common test patterns, not mandatory syntax for every test. Examples: https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/c0a4545202fcfa27f3fac30fb43d4ddf5ed432bd and https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/f76d3fa1c71103e8d522be22f6391667adf760b7
- Added code in 38 commits includes `/**` documentation blocks, including JSDoc in JavaScript. Review D329282 asked that a return description say what is returned; the landed `MockServer.items()` comment names both tuple elements. https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D329282 and https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/4f0a6139fedb0ffbfb9a1aeb667c0ca695d41a50
- Tests commonly assert observable state with a specific failure message and clean up changed prefs, servers, or windows. A review on D324413 asked for separate assertions so failures report their values; the landed compose test uses separate alignment and size checks. https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D324413 and https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/f76d3fa1c71103e8d522be22f6391667adf760b7

## Supported, scoped lessons

- Keep credentials tied to their intended site or origin through discovery and redirects. The CalDAV, ICS, and CardDAV commits add checks and tests for same-site and cross-site paths. Some linked reviews are restricted, so this lesson rests on landed code and tests: https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/b710d46b16ceb83a0a6793fd7d82ba839be3bf22 and https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/c0a4545202fcfa27f3fac30fb43d4ddf5ed432bd
- Preserve user choices across retry and avoid file-name collisions after sanitizing names. Review D329882 raised loss of chosen name and filter on failed save; landed `MessageSaver.saveAs()` keeps them. Review D329734 raised two sanitized attachments mapping to one file; landed code assigns distinct names before saving. https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D329882 and https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D329734
- For an accessible custom control, test keyboard use, focus, and ARIA state as behavior, not just attributes. D320309 raised held-arrow performance and the surprising difference between resize direction and `aria-orientation`; landed code comments on the latter and groups resize events around a key press. https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D320309 and https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/b0e1ab526d374d85c3fb436e3d3005a5390cf088
- Explain code that looks wrong but is required by a contract. The `aria-orientation` comment in D320309 is one example. D329689 requested a comment for a user-cancel path. These are examples, not a rule to comment every branch. https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D320309 and https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D329689

## Review use

Treat comments as evidence and inspect the landed code before turning them into a rule. D325184 contains explicit disagreement about broad `try/catch` removal; do not encode either side as a Thunderbird-wide rule. Distinguish a bot finding, an author explanation, a reviewer nit, and an accepted change. For a code-comment request, point to the exact misleading or missing contract and suggest the information the comment should carry. Match syntax and naming in the nearby component; use project formatters for mechanical style.

This batch shows work on credential boundaries, Exchange and Graph support, keyboard accessibility, and removal of old locale resources. That is a snapshot of recent work, not a published roadmap.
